title: Inheritance and Witness
premise: Dominic Dunmore, the cathedral's reclusive archivist, receives two letters in the same post: one confessing to a murder committed thirty years ago inside the locked crypt, the other promising a second death at the anniversary dinner of the parish restoration society. As Dominic digs into the restricted case file they were never meant to see, they realize the killer is someone who has read every page—perhaps someone who helped write them. The confession letter is bait, and Dominic's own buried memory of that night is the hook. In the crypt beneath the anniversary dinner, Dominic turns the archive itself into a trap, forcing the killer to confess before witnesses, and chooses testimony over silence: justice outside the law, paid for with the last of their invisibility.
about_author: Jonah Ashgrove spent a decade cataloguing municipal archives in coastal England before turning to fiction full-time. Their novels are known for quiet protagonists, ecclesiastical settings, and crimes that hinge on what paperwork remembers.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. While cataloguing bequests, Dominic opens twin letters: a detailed confession to the 1994 crypt murder of verger Ada Quill, and a second note promising 'the next glass raised will be her toast.' The handwriting on both matches documents in the cathedral's own files. Emotional beat: dread blooming in a life built on routine—the invisible archivist suddenly addressed by name.

chapters.title: The File That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic finds the original investigation file misfiled under a false donor name—someone hid it deliberately. The locked crypt was sealed from inside; the coroner ruled accident. A marginal note in the file uses a phrase from the letters word for word. Emotional beat: the thrill of forbidden knowledge curdling as Dominic realizes whoever planted the file wanted it found now.

chapters.title: What the Stones Kept
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, flashback interleave. Dominic confronts their own fragmented memory: as a child, they saw someone leave the crypt stairwell the night Ada died—and said nothing, because saying anything would have exposed their family. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing; survival was bought with silence, and the price is now due.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic surveys the restoration society's surviving founders—Canon Ellery, benefactor Marguerite Voss, retired detective Saul Breck—all slated for the anniversary dinner. Each deflects questions about Ada with rehearsed ease, but one of them flinches at the phrase from the margin note. Emotional beat: paranoia; every ally becomes a suspect, every courtesy a mask.

chapters.title: A Third Letter
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A third letter arrives, quoting Dominic's childhood statement to police—a statement that was never filed. The writer knows about the witness who stayed silent. It offers a bargain: identify yourself at the dinner, or the next confession names you instead. Emotional beat: terror and fury fused; the killer isn't taunting the police, they're recruiting Dominic.

chapters.title: Breck's Cold Case
chapters.summary: POV alternating Dominic and Breck. Retired Detective Breck, ashamed of the rushed verdict, quietly reopens his notes and confirms the crypt door was bolted from within—meaning either suicide, an accomplice, or a lie in the file itself. He and Dominic form an uneasy alliance, each hiding what they know. Emotional beat: two keepers of secrets recognizing each other across the table.

chapters.title: The Donor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Following money, Dominic discovers Ada was about to expose embezzlement of restoration funds the week she died—and the ledger pages were torn out by someone with archival access. Only four people could have entered the archive undetected over thirty years. Emotional beat: revelation sharpening into focus; the crime was administrative, intimate, and ongoing.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Funeral
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. On the eve of the dinner, Dominic stages the crypt: restoring the torn ledger, rigging the archive's old dictaphone system, and sending an anonymous summons designed to make the killer come verify the evidence themselves. Breck stands watch above. Emotional beat: cold resolve; the invisible archivist finally acts, trading safety for a snare.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. During the anniversary dinner, Canon Ellery raises the promised glass—and Dominic plays Ada's recovered recording through the hall's speakers, naming the embezzlement and the murder. Ellery flees to the crypt to destroy the ledger and walks into Breck and the assembled guests. Emotional beat: climax; confession dragged into light, the trap sprung on the man who weaponized the file.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Ellery, exposed but not yet arrested, bargains; Dominic refuses a private deal and gives a formal witness statement, finally speaking the childhood truth aloud. The crypt is unsealed and Ada properly buried. Dominic remains archivist—but no longer invisible, no longer silent. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; justice outside the law cost Dominic their shelter, and bought back their soul.
